content.title: About
content.content: Sweetened condensed milk is a thick, sweet dairy product made by evaporating whole milk and adding sugar. It has a creamy texture, caramel-like aroma, and is widely used in desserts, beverages, and confectionery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Condensed milk was invented in the United States in the late 19th century as a way to preserve milk for long periods.
In the Soviet Union its popularity surged after the 1960s with the brand “Sgushchenka”.
Sugar not only sweetens but also stabilizes the product, preventing crystallization.
It is a key ingredient in traditional treats like “ice cream‑condensed milk” and “medovik”.
An opened can can be kept in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days without quality loss.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: High sugar and fat content provides a quick source of calories, useful for increased energy needs.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: The dairy component supplies calcium and phosphorus, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Some brands fortify the milk with vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Growth‑supporting nutrients
items.content: Milk proteins contribute to tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to weight gain, tooth decay, and elevated blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein may react to the product.

items.title: Preservatives in some brands
items.content: Certain variants contain additives that may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use sweetened condensed milk in baking (cakes, cookies), beverages (coffee, tea, smoothies), desserts (ice cream, fruit salads) and as a sweet filling for pancakes or crepes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep the product in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or discoloration.
